subsystems.name: Collector elements
subsystems.role: vast numbers of very thin solar collectors, each as light as possible per square metre.

subsystems.name: Orbital constellation control
subsystems.role: keeps millions of elements in stable, non-colliding, phase-coordinated orbits.

subsystems.name: Transmitter phased arrays
subsystems.role: steers and focuses a microwave beam electronically by controlling the phase of thousands of small emitters.

subsystems.name: Receiver hub (rectenna)
subsystems.role: converts the incoming beam back into electricity at a single collection point.

subsystems.name: Manufacturing and material supply
subsystems.role: builds collectors without launching them from Earth.

subsystems.name: Beam command and safety
subsystems.role: maintains phase coherence and prevents the beam from drifting onto anything else.

buildSteps.title: Survey a feedstock
buildSteps.detail: Identify a near-Earth asteroid or lunar regolith deposit whose metals and silicon can be turned into collector mass.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate beaming at growing scale
buildSteps.detail: Prove microwave power transmission from a small emitter to a rectenna, then from orbit to a ground station, measuring end-to-end efficiency.

buildSteps.title: Close the manufacturing loop in space
buildSteps.detail: Show that robots can mine, refine and fabricate a working collector using only off-Earth material and solar power.

buildSteps.title: Build the first elements
buildSteps.detail: Assemble a handful of collectors, each perhaps hundreds of metres across, and put them in a coordinated orbit.

buildSteps.title: Form a demonstration cluster
buildSteps.detail: Grow to tens or hundreds of elements, phasing their beams together and holding formation for years without intervention.

buildSteps.title: Scale by replication
buildSteps.detail: Each generation of collectors builds the next from asteroid material, so the population grows without proportional Earth launches.

buildSteps.title: Place the receiver hub
buildSteps.detail: Site a rectenna and processing station at a stable point, such as a Lagrange point or a Sun-orbiting station, where the combined beam is delivered.

buildSteps.title: Operate the swarm
buildSteps.detail: Manage the rising infrared heat load the swarm re-radiates, clear orbital debris, and keep the beam safely pointed for decades.

prerequisites.why: kilowatt-to-tens-of-kilowatts transmissions over kilometres have been demonstrated; gigawatt-scale orbital beaming has not.

prerequisites.tech: Very low-cost access to space and in-space manufacturing
prerequisites.why: launching this much mass from Earth's surface is not economically or energetically plausible.
millions of elements must be built and maintained with no crews.
ungoverned swarms would collide, and collisions would cascade.

prerequisites.tech: Phased-array beam steering at very large baselines
prerequisites.why: phase-locking thousands of emitters into one coherent beam is demonstrated on small scales only.

pathway.milestone: laboratory and short-range microwave power-beaming demonstrations, plus small solar-power-satellite studies
an orbital solar power satellite beaming useful power to a ground rectenna
pathway.unlocks: proof that space-to-Earth energy transfer works at scale.

pathway.milestone: collectors and structures manufactured from asteroid or lunar material
pathway.unlocks: growth in orbit that is not capped by launch mass.

pathway.milestone: a self-expanding constellation orbiting the Sun
pathway.unlocks: capture of a large fraction of stellar output — and, as a by-product, an infrared excess that astronomers could look for as a sign of other civilisations.
